title: Grandma Was Right

pre.en: What did Tom do after he tried the bitter melon?
pre.zh: Tom 尝了苦瓜以后做了什么？
options: He pulled a face and left.
He drank a glass of water.
He said it was too salty.

intro: 一个新概念式的小故事：小陈小时候被奶奶逼着吃苦瓜，二十多年后在伦敦又遇上了它。读的时候留意 tend to 和 be likely to：说「一般会、很可能会」，不像 always 那样把话说死；否定是 tend not to 和 be unlikely to。结尾 Tom 的评价是个笑点。

sentences.en: When Chen was a boy, he couldn't stand bitter melon.
sentences.zh: 小陈小时候，最受不了的就是苦瓜。

sentences.en: It's a long green vegetable, and it tastes exactly like its name.
sentences.zh: 那是一种长长的绿色蔬菜，味道跟名字一模一样。

sentences.en: His grandma cooked it every Sunday, and he had to eat three pieces before he could leave the table.
sentences.zh: 奶奶每个星期天都做，他得吃完三块才能下桌。

sentences.en: Every time, he'd pull a face as if she'd given him medicine.
sentences.zh: 每回他都一脸嫌弃，好像奶奶喂他吃的是药。

sentences.en: She was always patient with him.
sentences.zh: 奶奶对他一直很有耐心。

sentences.en: When he was eight, she showed him how to cook it himself: first salt it, then squeeze it.
sentences.zh: 他八岁那年，奶奶教他自己做：先用盐腌，再把水挤掉。

sentences.en: He soon got the hang of it, but he still wouldn't eat it.
sentences.zh: 他很快就学会了，可还是不肯吃。

sentences.en: "Kids tend to hate bitter food," Lily said when he told her the story.
sentences.zh: 他跟 Lily 讲起这事，Lily 说：「小孩一般都讨厌苦的东西。」

sentences.en: "Most people grow out of it."
sentences.zh: 「大多数人长大了就好了。」

sentences.en: "It's an acquired taste, like coffee or beer."
sentences.zh: 「这种味道得慢慢才吃得惯，跟咖啡、啤酒一样。」

sentences.en: "As far as I know, nobody in our family likes it except Grandma," Chen said.
sentences.zh: 「据我所知，咱家除了奶奶，没人爱吃这个，」小陈说。

sentences.en: "I do," said Lily.
sentences.zh: 「我爱吃啊，」Lily 说。

sentences.en: Chen had put off cooking it for years.
sentences.zh: 这道菜小陈拖了好多年都没做。

sentences.en: But with Lily around, he'd started making the dishes they grew up with.
sentences.zh: 不过 Lily 来了以后，他又做起了兄妹俩小时候常吃的那些菜。

sentences.en: Last week he found bitter melon in a Chinese supermarket in Bayswater for £3.20.
sentences.zh: 上周，他在贝斯沃特的一家中国超市找到了苦瓜，3.2 英镑。

sentences.en: He carried it home on the bus with six eggs.
sentences.zh: 他坐公交车把苦瓜和六个鸡蛋一起带回了家。

sentences.en: The bus was packed, so the eggs were likely to break.
sentences.zh: 车上挤得要命，鸡蛋多半要碎。

sentences.en: But somehow, they got home in one piece.
sentences.zh: 可不知怎么的，鸡蛋一个都没碎，平平安安到了家。

sentences.en: He did it Grandma's way.
sentences.zh: 他完全照奶奶教的来做。

sentences.en: He left the slices in salt for twenty minutes, and in the meantime, he beat the eggs.
sentences.zh: 苦瓜片用盐腌二十分钟，趁这工夫，他把鸡蛋打散。

sentences.en: To his surprise, it wasn't bad at all.
sentences.zh: 没想到，味道一点都不差。

sentences.en: He cleared his plate, which his grandma would never believe.
sentences.zh: 他把盘子吃得干干净净——奶奶要是知道了，肯定不信。

sentences.en: He made it again on Thursday, and again on Sunday, and slowly it grew on him.
sentences.zh: 周四他又做了一次，周日又做了一次，慢慢地，他还真喜欢上这个味道了。

sentences.en: Tom tends not to eat anything green apart from frozen peas.
sentences.zh: Tom 一般除了冷冻豌豆，绿色的东西一概不吃。

sentences.en: So he wasn't likely to enjoy this.
sentences.zh: 所以这道菜他多半不会喜欢。

sentences.en: But he usually goes along with Chen's experiments.
sentences.zh: 不过小陈的各种实验，他通常都肯配合。

sentences.en: On Sunday, Chen made him take a bite.
sentences.zh: 周日，小陈让他尝了一口。

sentences.en: Tom chewed for a long time while Chen and Lily watched.
sentences.zh: Tom 嚼了好半天，小陈和 Lily 就在旁边盯着。

sentences.en: "It tastes like a cucumber that's angry with you," he said at last.
sentences.zh: 「吃起来像一根在生你气的黄瓜，」他终于开口了。

sentences.en: Then he asked for more.
sentences.zh: 然后他又要了一份。

cards.note: to dislike someone or something very much
cards.tip: 后面接名词或 doing：can't stand waiting。过去用 couldn't stand；这里的 stand 是「忍受」，不是「站」。
cards.example: I can't stand people who talk during films.

cards.zh: （因为不喜欢）皱起脸；露出嫌弃的表情
cards.note: to make an expression with your face to show that you do not like something
cards.tip: 这里是嫌弃、不情愿的表情，不是逗人笑的「做鬼脸」（那个常说 pull funny faces）。英式说法，美式多说 make a face；冲某人做是 pull a face at sb。
cards.example: My son pulled a face when he saw the broccoli.

cards.note: to stay calm and not get angry when someone is slow or makes mistakes
挤柠檬汁：squeeze a lemon。
to learn how to do something, especially after some practice
bitter melon 就是苦瓜；也可以说人「心里不服、怨恨」：feel bitter about sth。

cards.zh: （要慢慢才会喜欢的）独特口味
cards.note: something that you do not like at first but start to like after you try it more
cards.tip: 常说食物、饮料，也可以说音乐、人：His humour is an acquired taste。
cards.example: Strong black tea is an acquired taste.

cards.note: used to say that you think something is true, but you are not completely sure
cards.tip: 说的人留了余地：我知道的是这样，但不保证。
cards.example: As far as I know, the shop is still open.

cards.note: to decide to do something later than planned
口语里常说 packed with people；也说 crowded。
not broken or damaged
cards.tip: 也可以说人平安无事：We got home in one piece。
cards.example: The parcel arrived in one piece, thank goodness.

cards.note: 一片面包是 a slice of bread；也能当动词「切片」。
in the period of time between two events
beat 本义是「打、击败」；beat–beat–beaten。
used to say that something was not what you expected
to eat all the food on your plate
cards.tip: your 要跟着主语换：he cleared his plate。clear the table 是「收拾餐桌」。
cards.example: The kids cleared their plates in five minutes.

cards.note: if something grows on you, you start to like it more and more
cards.tip: 主语是东西，宾语是人：It grew on me，不说 I grew on it。grow 的过去式 grew，过去分词 grown。
cards.example: I didn't like the song at first, but it's grown on me.

cards.note: to accept something or agree with someone, often without saying what you really think
cards.tip: 常带「不太情愿但不反对」的意思；go 的过去式 went。
cards.example: I didn't love the plan, but I went along with it.

cards.note: to put some food in your mouth and bite off a piece
cards.tip: 咬哪个用 of：take a bite of sth。喝一口是 take a sip。
cards.example: Can I take a bite of your sandwich?

cards.note: 口香糖是 chewing gum。
as cool as a cucumber 是「非常冷静」。
